q: (Only Allaah knows the correct meaning of these letters).
This is a Book, the verses of which have been consolidated
(are excellently structured and are comprehensive and eloquent)
(to make its meaning clear to man. It comes)
v.s: Alif, Lām, Rā. [This is] a Book whose verses are perfected and then presented in detail from [one who is] Wise and Acquainted
v.c: Alif-Lãm-Ra. ˹This is˺ a Book whose verses are well perfected and then fully explained. ˹It is˺ from the One ˹Who is˺ All-Wise, All-Aware.

m: and a bearer of glad tidings
q: (The message that this Qur'aan bears is that you should)
(about Allaah's punishment if you commit kufr and sin)
(that you will have Jannah for Imaan and good deeds).
v.s: [Through a messenger, saying], "Do not worship except God. Indeed, I am to you from Him a warner and a bringer of good tidings,"
v.c: ˹Tell them, O Prophet,˺ “Worship none but Allah. Surely I am a warner and deliverer of good news to you from Him.

q: (The message of the Qur'aan is also that you should)
Seek forgiveness from your Rabb and then turn to Him
He will then grant you enjoyment
then I truly fear the punishment of a serious day for you
v.s: And [saying], "Seek forgiveness of your Lord and repent to Him, [and] He will let you enjoy a good provision for a specified term and give every doer of favor his favor [i.e., reward]. But if you turn away, then indeed, I fear for you the punishment of a great Day.
v.c: And seek your Lord’s forgiveness and turn to Him in repentance. He will grant you a good provision for an appointed term and graciously reward the doers of good. But if you turn away, then I truly fear for you the torment of a formidable Day.

q: To Allaah shall you be returned
He has power over all things
(and has the ability to take you to task for all the wrong you (do)).
v.s: To God is your return, and He is over all things competent."
v.c: To Allah is your return. And He is Most Capable of everything.”

q: turn their chests so that they may hide from Him. Behold!
(thinking that they are hiding themselves from Allaah),
He knows what they hide as well as what they disclose. Undoubtedly, He has knowledge of the secrets of their
v.s: Unquestionably, they [i.e., the disbelievers] turn away their breasts to hide themselves from him. Unquestionably, [even] when they cover themselves in their clothing, He [i.e., God] knows what they conceal and what they declare. Indeed, He is Knowing of that within the breasts.
v.c: Indeed, they enfold ˹what is in˺ their hearts, ˹trying˺ to hide it from Him! But even when they cover themselves with their clothes, He knows what they conceal and what they reveal. Surely He knows best what is ˹hidden˺ in the heart.

q: The responsibility of sustaining every creature on earth rests with Allaah. He knows the place where they will stay
(for a longer period in Jannah or Jahannam)
and the place where they will be kept in trust
(for a shorter period in the world/the grave).
v.s: And there is no creature on earth but that upon God is its provision, and He knows its place of dwelling and place of storage. All is in a clear register.
v.c: There is no moving creature on earth whose provision is not guaranteed by Allah. And He knows where it lives and where it is laid to rest. All is ˹written˺ in a perfect Record.

q: Who created the heavens and the earth in six days when His throne was upon water, to test which of you carries out better actions

(Allaah created these things so that by seeing them, man can recognise Allaah's power and oneness and by using them, man can be thankful to Him. While many passed the test by recognising Him and thanking Him, others did not).
Surely if you say, “Indeed you will be resurrected
after death,” those who commit kufr will definitely reply, “This
v.s: And it is He who created the heavens and the earth in six days - and His Throne had been upon water - that He might test you as to which of you is best in deed. But if you say, "Indeed, you are resurrected after death," those who disbelieve will surely say, "This is not but obvious magic."
v.c: He is the One Who created the heavens and the earth in six Days—and His Throne was upon the waters—in order to test which of you is best in deeds. And if you ˹O Prophet˺ say, “Surely you will ˹all˺ be raised up after death,” the disbelievers will certainly say, “That is nothing but pure magic!”

q: Indeed, if We have to postpone the punishment from them for a little while, they will certainly say
“What holds it back?” Behold! The day when it will afflict them, it will not be turned away from them and
v.s: And if We hold back from them the punishment for a limited time, they will surely say, "What detains it?" Unquestionably, on the Day it comes to them, it will not be averted from them, and they will be enveloped by what they used to ridicule.
v.c: And if We delay their punishment until an appointed time, they will definitely say, “What is holding it back?” Indeed, on the Day it overtakes them, it will not be averted from them, and they will be overwhelmed by what they used to ridicule.

q: Undoubtedly, if We allow man to taste of Our mercy
(a favour such as wealth or good health)
and then snatch it away from him, he will certainly be despondent
(failing to realise that it was Allaah Who granted him the favour in the first place).
v.s: And if We give man a taste of mercy from Us and then We withdraw it from him, indeed, he is despairing and ungrateful.
v.c: If We give people a taste of Our mercy then take it away from them, they become utterly desperate, ungrateful.

q: If We allow him to taste any bounty after hardship had afflicted him, he will certainly say, “All difficulties have left me!”
(Instead of being grateful to Allaah and fulfilling Allaah's commands,)
He then becomes boastful and arrogant
(thinking that the bounty was earned through his own resourcefulness and effort).
v.s: But if We give him a taste of favor after hardship has touched him, he will surely say, "Bad times have left me." Indeed, he is exultant and boastful -
v.c: But if We give them a taste of prosperity after being touched with adversity, they say, “My ills are gone,” and become totally prideful and boastful,

q: and who do good acts. For them shall be forgiveness and an immense reward
(because they are always grateful to Allaah and are patient).
v.s: Except for those who are patient and do righteous deeds; those will have forgiveness and great reward.
v.c: except those who patiently endure and do good. It is they who will have forgiveness and a mighty reward.

q: some of the commands that have been revealed to you
(fearing that the Mushrikeen will mock them),
that your heart grieves because they
say, “Why is a treasure not sent down to him or why does an angel not accompany him
(to prove that he is a Nabi)?”
You are but one who warns
(people about the consequences of kufr and sin. It is not your duty to force people to accept Imaan. You should therefore not grieve when they refuse to accept).
Allaah has control over all things
(Allaah decides whether people should have Imaan or not).
v.s: Then would you possibly leave [out] some of what is revealed to you, or is your breast constrained by it because they say, "Why has there not been sent down to him a treasure or come with him an angel?" But you are only a warner. And God is Disposer of all things.
v.c: Perhaps you ˹O Prophet˺ may wish to give up some of what is revealed to you and may be distressed by it because they say, “If only a treasure had been sent down to him, or an angel had come with him!” You are only a warner, and Allah is the Trustee of All Affairs.

q: and, besides Allaah, call whoever you can

(in your claim).” (If the Qur'aan had been “fabricated” as the Kuffaar claim, then let alone one Surah, they should certainly be able to produce ten Surahs similar to those of the Qur'aan because there had been many Arabic speakers who were masters of the language.)
v.s: Or do they say, "He invented it"? Say, "Then bring ten sūrahs like it that have been invented and call upon [for assistance] whomever you can besides God, if you should be truthful."
v.c: Or do they say, “He has fabricated this ˹Quran˺!”? Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Produce ten fabricated sûrahs like it and seek help from whoever you can —other than Allah—if what you say is true!”

q: If they do not respond to you
(if they are unable to produce anything similar to the Surahs of the Qur'aan),
has been revealed by Allaah's knowledge
(and power without any contribution by anyone else),
and that there is no Ilaah but Allaah
(because no other being can assist you to produce anything to match the Qur'aan).
(obey this proof and accept Islaam since the truth of the Qur'aan and the Prophethood of Rasulullaah ﷺ have been proven to you)?
v.s: And if they do not respond to you - then know that it [i.e., the Qur’ān] was revealed with the knowledge of God and that there is no deity except Him. Then, would you [not] be Muslims?
v.c: But if your helpers fail you, then know that it has been revealed with the knowledge of Allah, and that there is no god ˹worthy of worship˺ except Him! Will you ˹not˺ then submit ˹to Allah˺?

q: Whoever desires the life of this world and its splendour
(luxurious without a concern for the Aakhirah which they do not believe in),
We shall grant them the full rewards for their
deeds in this very world and they will not be wronged
(they will not be given less than they deserve).
v.s: Whoever desires the life of this world and its adornments - We fully repay them for their deeds therein, and they therein will not be deprived.
v.c: Whoever desires ˹only˺ this worldly life and its luxuries, We will pay them in full for their deeds in this life—nothing will be left out.

q: They are the ones who shall have only
the Fire for themselves in the Aakhirah. Whatever
they did in the world will be lost to them
(because they will see no rewards for these in the Aakhirah where they will require them most. This is because they craved only for worldly possessions).
v.s: Those are the ones for whom there is not in the Hereafter but the Fire. And lost is what they did therein, and worthless is what they used to do.
v.c: It is they who will have nothing in the Hereafter except the Fire. Their efforts in this life will be fruitless and their deeds will be useless.

q: (the one who is like this, be equal to)
from his Rabb, which is followed
(Jibra'eel ﵊ who brought the Qur'aan from Allaah, as well as the fact that no human can produce anything like it)
before it by the Book of Moosa ﵊
and was a mercy to people
(The Torah mentioned the coming of Rasulullaah ﷺ and the Qur'aan).
(who are steadfast on the teachings of the Qur'aan truly)
believe in it. Whoever rejects it from the groups
is his promised abode. So do not be in doubt about it. It is indeed the truth from your Rabb, but most people do not know
v.s: So is one who [stands] upon a clear evidence from his Lord [like the aforementioned]? And a witness from Him follows it, and before it was the Scripture of Moses to lead and as mercy. Those [believers in the former revelations] believe in it [i.e., the Qur’ān]. But whoever disbelieves in it from the [various] factions - the Fire is his promised destination. So be not in doubt about it. Indeed, it is the truth from your Lord, but most of the people do not believe.
v.c: ˹Can these people be compared to˺ those ˹believers˺ who stand on clear proof from their Lord, backed by ˹the Quran as˺ a witness from Him, and preceded by the Book of Moses ˹which was revealed˺ as a guide and mercy? It is those ˹believers˺ who have faith in it. But whoever from the ˹disbelieving˺ groups rejects it, the Fire will be their destiny. So do not be in doubt of it. It is certainly the truth from your Lord, but most people do not believe.

q: Who can be more unjust than he who invents lies against Allaah
(by saying that Allaah has children and partners)?
These people will be presented before their Rabb, and the witnesses
(the recording angels, their limbs and the earth)
will say, “These are the ones who attributed lies to their Rabb.” Behold! The curse of Allaah is on the liars
v.s: And who is more unjust than he who invents a lie about God? Those will be presented before their Lord, and the witnesses will say, "These are the ones who lied against their Lord." Unquestionably, the curse of God is upon the wrongdoers.
v.c: Who does more wrong than those who fabricate lies against Allah? They will be brought before their Lord, and the witnesses will say, “These are the ones who lied against their Lord.” Surely Allah’s condemnation is upon the wrongdoers,

q: (ways to make it seem as if there is)
v.s: Who averted [people] from the way of God and sought to make it [seem] deviant while they, concerning the Hereafter, were disbelievers.
v.c: who hinder ˹others˺ from Allah’s Path, striving to make it ˹appear˺ crooked, and disbelieve in the Hereafter.

q: Such people are not likely to escape
on earth, and besides Allaah they shall not have any helpers
(because in addition to their own rejection, they also convinced others to reject).
They have neither the ability to hear
(the truth because they do not want to hear or see it).
v.s: Those were not causing failure [to God] on earth, nor did they have besides God any protectors. For them the punishment will be multiplied. They were not able to hear, nor did they see.
v.c: They will never frustrate Allah on earth, and they will have no protector besides Allah. Their punishment will be multiplied, for they failed to hear or see ˹the truth˺.

q: These are the ones who have
(will be unable to assist them in the Aakhirah).
v.s: Those are the ones who will have lost themselves, and lost from them is what they used to invent.
v.c: It is they who have ruined themselves, and whatever ˹gods˺ they fabricated will fail them.

q: Without doubt, they will be the worst losers in the Aakhirah!
v.s: Assuredly, it is they in the Hereafter who will be the greatest losers.
v.c: Without a doubt, they will be the worst losers in the Hereafter.

q: Surely those who have Imaan, who do righteous acts and who humble themselves before their Rabb
(fulfil all His commands and worship Him only),
these are the residents of Jannah, where they shall live forever.
v.s: Indeed, they who have believed and done righteous deeds and humbled themselves to their Lord - those are the companions of Paradise; they will abide eternally therein.
v.c: Surely those who believe, do good, and humble themselves before their Lord will be the residents of Paradise. They will be there forever.

q: The example of the two groups
(those who have Imaan and those who do not believe)
who can see and hear. Can the two be equal?
(Seeing the stark difference between the Mu'min and Kaafir)
(will you not ponder and accept Islaam)?
v.s: The example of the two parties is like the blind and deaf, and the seeing and hearing. Are they equal in comparison? Then, will you not remember?
v.c: The example of these two parties is that of the blind and the deaf, compared to the seeing and the hearing. Can the two be equal? Will you not then be mindful?

q: “Undoubtedly I am one who clearly warns you...’
v.s: And We had certainly sent Noah to his people, [saying], "Indeed, I am to you a clear warner
v.c: Surely We sent Noah to his people. ˹He said,˺ “Indeed, I am sent to you with a clear warning

q: I truly fear for you the punishment of a painful day.”
v.s: That you not worship except God. Indeed, I fear for you the punishment of a painful day."
v.c: that you should worship none but Allah. I truly fear for you the torment of a painful Day.”

q: of his nation said, We consider you to be a mere human like ourselves and we see that only those people follow you who are of low class and who are simple minded. We see no superiority in you over us
(we therefore see no reason why we should follow you).

(and will therefore not follow you).” (Like many nations, the people of Nooh ﵊ failed to realise that a Nabi has to be a human being. Angels are unable to be effective as Ambiyaa because they do not have the same needs as humans have and can therefore not identify with humans. Nevertheless, even if Allaah did send angels as Ambiyaa to humans, stubborn people would have rejected them on the grounds that they are not human.)
v.s: So the eminent among those who disbelieved from his people said, "We do not see you but as a man like ourselves, and we do not see you followed except by those who are the lowest of us [and] at first suggestion. And we do not see in you over us any merit; rather, we think you are liars."
v.c: The disbelieving chiefs of his people said, “We see you only as a human being like ourselves, and we see that no one follows you except the lowliest among us, who do so ˹hastily˺ without thinking. We do not see anything that makes ˹all of˺ you any better than us. In fact, we think you are liars.”

m: should We compel you (to accept) it
q: Nooh ﵊ replied, “O my people! Tell me. If I am on
(a miracle which proves that I am Allaah's Nabi)
and He has granted me a mercy
from Himself that is unclear to you
(because you are adamant that a Nabi has to be an angel),
can we force it onto you when you disapprove of it?”
(The duty of a Nabi is only to convey the message to people and not to force them. People are required to accept his message willingly.)
v.s: He said, "O my people, have you considered: if I should be upon clear evidence from my Lord while He has given me mercy from Himself but it has been made unapparent to you, should we force it upon you while you are averse to it?
v.c: He said, “O my people! Consider if I stand on a clear proof from my Lord and He has blessed me with a mercy from Himself, which you fail to see. Should we ˹then˺ force it on you against your will?

q: “O my people! I do not ask you for any wealth. My reward is with my Rabb, and I cannot discard
(Nooh ﵊ said this when the people expressed that they would follow him only if he disassociated himself from his followers who were poor).
(after death when they will be able to complain to Allaah about those who discarded them).
However, I deem (see) you to be foolish
(people who make foolish statements, who speak without proof).'
v.s: And O my people, I ask not of you for it any wealth. My reward is not but from God. And I am not one to drive away those who have believed. Indeed, they will meet their Lord, but I see that you are a people behaving ignorantly.
v.c: O my people! I do not ask you for a payment for this ˹message˺. My reward is only from Allah. And I will never dismiss the believers, for they will surely meet their Lord. But I can see that you are a people acting ignorantly.

q: “O my people! Who will assist me
v.s: And O my people, who would protect me from God if I drove them away? Then will you not be reminded?
v.c: O my people! Who would protect me from Allah if I were to dismiss them? Will you not then be mindful?

q: “I do not say to you that I possess the treasures of Allaah
(I can neither produce miracles nor punishment as and when I please),
nor do I have knowledge of the unseen
nor do I say that I am an angel
and I cannot say concerning those whom you look down upon that Allaah will never grant them good. Allaah knows best what is in their hearts
(Allaah will elevate their status in the Aakhirah because of their Imaan).
I will certainly be of the
v.s: And I do not tell you that I have the depositories [containing the provision] of God or that I know the unseen, nor do I tell you that I am an angel, nor do I say of those upon whom your eyes look down that God will never grant them any good. God is most knowing of what is within their souls. Indeed, I would then be among the wrongdoers [i.e., the unjust]."
v.c: I do not say to you that I possess Allah’s treasuries or know the unseen, nor do I claim to be an angel, nor do I say that Allah will never grant goodness to those you look down upon. Allah knows best what is ˹hidden˺ within them. ˹If I did,˺ then I would truly be one of the wrongdoers.”

q: said, “O Nooh! You have disputed with us and disputed to a great extent
you promise us if you are of the truthful ones.”
v.s: They said, "O Noah, you have disputed [i.e., opposed] us and been frequent in dispute of us. So bring us what you threaten us, if you should be of the truthful."
v.c: They protested, “O Noah! You have argued with us far too much, so bring upon us what you threaten us with, if what you say is true.”

q: He said, “Only Allaah will bring it
you will be unable to escape.”
v.s: He said, "God will only bring it to you if He wills, and you will not cause [Him] failure.
v.c: He responded, “It is Allah Who can bring it upon you if He wills, and then you will have no escape!

q: “My advice to you shall not benefit you if I intend to guide you while Allaah intends to send you astray
and to Him shall you be returned
(for reckoning after death).” (The Kuffaar of Makkah also made similar objections and therefore received the same replies.)
v.s: And my advice will not benefit you - although I wished to advise you - if God should intend to put you in error. He is your Lord, and to Him you will be returned."
v.c: My advice will not benefit you—no matter how hard I try—if Allah wills ˹for˺ you to stray. He is your Lord, and to Him you will ˹all˺ be returned.”

q: then the crime is mine and
(you are absolved from it just as)
I am absolved of the crime that you carry out
(your crime of rejecting Allaah's word and saying that it is mine).'
v.s: Or do they say [about Prophet Muhammad (صلى الله عليه وسلم)], "He invented it”? Say, “If I have invented it, then upon me is [the consequence of] my crime; but I am innocent of what [crimes] you commit.”
v.c: Or do they say, “He has fabricated this ˹Quran˺!”? Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “If I have done so, then I bear the burden of that sin! But I am free from your sinful accusation.”

q: It was revealed to Nooh ﵊ “None of your people shall ever have Imaan
but those who already have Imaan, so do not be grieved by what
v.s: And it was revealed to Noah that, "No one will believe from your people except those who have already believed, so do not be distressed by what they have been doing.
v.c: And it was revealed to Noah, “None of your people will believe except those who already have. So do not be distressed by what they have been doing.

q: and do not address Me regarding the oppressors
(do not intercede on behalf of any of the Mushrikeen).
(in the flood that is to come).”
v.s: And construct the ship under Our observation and Our inspiration and do not address Me concerning those who have wronged; indeed, they are [to be] drowned."
v.c: And build the Ark under Our ˹watchful˺ Eyes and directions, and do not plead with Me for those who have done wrong, for they will surely be drowned.”

q: continued to build the ark. Whenever the leaders of his people passed by him, they mocked him
(among other insults, they told him that he was foolish to build an ark when there was no water about).
said, “If you mock us, then we shall also
mock you just as you do to us.
v.s: And he constructed the ship, and whenever an assembly of the eminent of his people passed by him, they ridiculed him. He said, "If you ridicule us, then we will ridicule you just as you ridicule.
v.c: So he began to build the Ark, and whenever some of the chiefs of his people passed by, they mocked him. He said, “If you laugh at us, we will ˹soon˺ laugh at you similarly.

q: you shall come to know who will be afflicted by a humiliating
and to whom shall an eternal punishment come
v.s: And you are going to know who will get a punishment that will disgrace him [on earth] and upon whom will descend an enduring punishment [in the Hereafter]."
v.c: You will soon come to know who will be visited by a humiliating torment ˹in this life˺ and overwhelmed by an everlasting punishment ˹in the next˺.”

q: and water began to gush from the
(as a sign to Nooh ﵊ that the flood was imminent).
and your family; except those against whom the decision
(his wife and one of his sons);
With him, there were only a few
(Various reports cite different numbers, ranging from six to eighty-two.)
v.s: [So it was], until when Our command came and the oven overflowed, We said, "Load upon it [i.e., the ship] of each [creature] two mates and your family, except those about whom the word [i.e., decree] has preceded, and [include] whoever has believed." But none had believed with him, except a few.
v.c: And when Our command came and the oven burst ˹with water˺, We said ˹to Noah˺, “Take into the Ark a pair from every species along with your family—except those against whom the decree ˹to drown˺ has already been passed—and those who believe.” But none believed with him except for a few.

q: said, “Embark on it! With the name of Allaah shall it travel and anchor. Surely my Rabb is the Most Forgiving, the Most Merciful.”
v.s: And [Noah] said, “Embark therein; in the name of God is its course and its anchorage. Indeed, my Lord is Forgiving and Merciful.”
v.c: And he said, “Board it! In the Name of Allah it will sail and cast anchor. Surely my Lord is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.”

q: with them amid waves that were like mountains
(stood apart from them outside the ark)
saying, “O my son! Board with us and do not be of the Kaafiroon!”
v.s: And it sailed with them through waves like mountains, and Noah called to his son who was apart [from them], "O my son, come aboard with us and be not with the disbelievers."
v.c: And ˹so˺ the Ark sailed with them through waves like mountains. Noah called out to his son, who stood apart, “O my dear son! Come aboard with us and do not be with the disbelievers.”

q: He replied, “I shall shortly take refuge
on a mountain that will rescue
me from the water.” Nooh ﵊ said, “Today none can rescue
of Allaah except him on whom Allaah has
became of those who were drowned.
v.s: [But] he said, "I will take refuge on a mountain to protect me from the water." [Noah] said, "There is no protector today from the decree of God, except for whom He gives mercy." And the waves came between them, and he was among the drowned.
v.c: He replied, “I will take refuge on a mountain, which will protect me from the water.” Noah cried, “Today no one is protected from Allah’s decree except those to whom He shows mercy!” And the waves came between them, and his son was among the drowned.

q: “O Earth! Swallow your water and O sky! Stop
was over and the ark settled on Mount Judi. It was announced, “May the
v.s: And it was said, "O earth, swallow your water, and O sky, withhold [your rain]." And the water subsided, and the matter was accomplished, and it [i.e., the ship] came to rest on the [mountain of] Jūdiyy. And it was said, "Away with the wrongdoing people."
v.c: And it was said, “O earth! Swallow up your water. And O sky! Withhold ˹your rain˺.” The floodwater receded and the decree was carried out. The Ark rested on Mount Judi, and it was said, “Away with the wrongdoing people!”

q: Nooh ﵊ called to his Rabb saying
is from my family and indeed Your promise
(to rescue my family from the flood)
(Why was he then not blessed with Imaan and not saved from the flood?) (However,)
You are the Best of Judges
(there must therefore be good reason why You allowed him to drown).”
v.s: And Noah called to his Lord and said, "My Lord, indeed my son is of my family; and indeed, Your promise is true; and You are the most just of judges!"
v.c: Noah called out to his Lord, saying, “My Lord! Certainly my son is ˹also˺ of my family, Your promise is surely true, and You are the most just of all judges!”

q: Allaah said, “O Nooh! Indeed he was not from your family
(he was not destined to be a Mu'min like the others and therefore could not be saved).
so do not ask Me about that which you have no knowledge
(do not ask me to save him when you have no knowledge about his inner condition).
I advise you not to be of the ignorant
(those who make requests about another which they do not have knowledge).”
v.s: He said, "O Noah, indeed he is not of your family; indeed, he is [one whose] work was other than righteous, so ask Me not for that about which you have no knowledge. Indeed, I advise you, lest you be among the ignorant."
v.c: Allah replied, “O Noah! He is certainly not of your family—he was entirely of unrighteous conduct. So do not ask Me about what you have no knowledge of! I warn you so you do not fall into ignorance.”

m: and You have mercy on me
q: (Realising that he was wrong to ask about his son)
Nooh ﵊ said, “O my Rabb! I seek Your protection from asking You about things about which I have no knowledge. If You do not forgive me and have mercy on me, I will be of the losers.”
v.s: [Noah] said, "My Lord, I seek refuge in You from asking that of which I have no knowledge. And unless You forgive me and have mercy upon me, I will be among the losers."
v.c: Noah pleaded, “My Lord, I seek refuge in You from asking You about what I have no knowledge of, and unless You forgive me and have mercy on me, I will be one of the losers.”

q: with peace from Us and blessings upon you and upon those parties with you
(they and their progeny will benefit who accept Imaan).
And there shall be many parties
to whom We will grant enjoyment (in
and then subject them to a torturous
v.s: It was said, "O Noah, disembark in security from Us and blessings upon you and upon nations [descending] from those with you. But other nations [of them] We will grant enjoyment; then there will touch them from Us a painful punishment."
v.c: It was said, “O Noah! Disembark with Our peace and blessings on you and some of the descendants of those with you. As for the others, We will allow them ˹a brief˺ enjoyment, then they will be touched with a painful punishment from Us.”

q: of the unseen that We inspire you with
You and your people were unlikely to have knowledge about this before
(continue preaching Islaam and patiently bear the harassment and tortures of the Kuffaar just as Nooh ﵊ had done)!
Indeed the final outcome will be in favour of those who have Taqwa.
v.s: That is from the news of the unseen which We reveal to you, [O Muhammad]. You knew it not, neither you nor your people, before this. So be patient; indeed, the [best] outcome is for the righteous.
v.c: This is one of the stories of the unseen, which we reveal to you ˹O Prophet˺. Neither you nor your people knew it before this. So be patient! Surely the ultimate outcome belongs ˹only˺ to the righteous.

q: Aad We sent their brother Hood ﵊
Allaah. There is no Ilaah besides Him. You people are only lying
v.s: And to ʿAad [We sent] their brother Hūd. He said, "O my people, worship God; you have no deity other than Him. You are not but inventors [of falsehood].
v.c: And to the people of ’Âd We sent their brother Hûd. He said, “O my people! Worship Allah. You have no god other than Him. You do nothing but fabricate lies ˹against Allah˺.

q: “O my people! I do not ask you for any reward for
My reward is the responsibility of that Being Who created me. Do you not understand
(that there must be truth in my message if I am exerting myself so greatly without any ulterior motives)?”
v.s: O my people, I do not ask you for it [i.e., my advice] any reward. My reward is only from the one who created me. Then will you not reason?
v.c: O my people! I do not ask you for any reward for this ˹message˺. My reward is only from the One Who created me. Will you not then understand?

q: “O my people! Seek forgiveness from your Rabb, then turn to Him
He will then send abundant rains to you and add strength to your strength. And do not turn
v.s: And O my people, ask forgiveness of your Lord and then repent to Him. He will send [rain from] the sky upon you in showers and increase you in strength [added] to your strength. And do not turn away, [being] criminals."
v.c: And O my people! Seek your Lord’s forgiveness and turn to Him in repentance. He will shower you with rain in abundance, and add strength to your strength. So do not turn away, persisting in wickedness.”

q: They replied, “O Hood! You have not brought forth a proof
(a miracle to prove that you are a Nabi).
We will not leave our gods merely on your word
nor shall we believe in you
v.s: They said, "O Hūd, you have not brought us clear evidence, and we are not ones to leave our gods on your say-so. Nor are we believers in you.
v.c: They argued, “O Hûd! You have not given us any clear proof, and we will never abandon our gods upon your word, nor will we believe in you.
v.h: His People’s Response and His Argument

q: “All we have to say is that one of our gods has afflicted
He said, “I call Allaah to Witness and you
to witness that I am absolved
v.s: We only say that some of our gods have possessed you with evil [i.e., insanity]." He said, "Indeed, I call God to witness, and witness [yourselves] that I am free from whatever you associate with God
v.c: All we can say is that some of our gods have possessed you with evil.” He said, “I call Allah to witness, and you too bear witness, that I ˹totally˺ reject whatever you associate

q: ...apart from Allaah. So all of you may plot against me and do not grant me any respite.”
v.s: Other than Him. So plot against me all together; then do not give me respite.
v.c: with Him ˹in worship˺. So let all of you plot against me without delay!

q: on Allaah, Who is my Rabb and your Rabb. He has
control of the forelocks of every creature
(complete control of them. You can therefore do me no harm without His permission).
Indeed, my Rabb is on the straight path
(the path of truth and justice so walk on it and you will meet Allaah).”
v.s: Indeed, I have relied upon God, my Lord and your Lord. There is no creature but that He holds its forelock [i.e., controls it]. Indeed, my Lord is on a path [that is] straight.”
v.c: I have put my trust in Allah—my Lord and your Lord. There is no living creature that is not completely under His control. Surely my Lord’s Way is perfect justice.

m: And my Lord will give succession
And my Lord will give succession
q: I have certainly conveyed to you that
with which I have been sent to you. My Rabb
(does not need you to worship Him because He)
can substitute you with another nation
you will not be able to harm Him in the least. Without doubt, my Rabb is Aware of all things.”
v.s: But if they turn away, [say], “I have already conveyed that with which I was sent to you. My Lord will give succession to a people other than you, and you will not harm Him at all. Indeed my Lord is, over all things, Guardian.”
v.c: But if you turn away, I have already delivered to you what I have been sent with. My Lord will replace you with others. You are not harming Him in the least. Indeed, my Lord is a ˹vigilant˺ Keeper over all things.”

q: Hood ﵊ and those with him by Our mercy. We
rescued him from a severe punishment
(a severe windstorm that lasted for 7 nights and) 8 days).
v.s: And when Our command came, We saved Hūd and those who believed with him, by mercy from Us; and We saved them from a harsh punishment.
v.c: When Our command came, We rescued Hûd and those who believed with him by a mercy from Us, saving them from a harsh torment.

q: This was the Aad! They rejected the Aayaat
of their Rabb, disobeyed His Rusul
(disobeying one Rasool is equal to disobeying all the Rusul because they all conveyed the message of Towheed),
followed the instruction of every obstinate tyrant.
v.s: And that was ʿAad, who rejected the signs of their Lord and disobeyed His messengers and followed the order of every obstinate tyrant.
v.c: That was ’Âd. They denied the signs of their Lord, disobeyed His messengers, and followed the command of every stubborn tyrant.

q: was made to follow them in this world and in the Aakhirah as well. Behold! The Aad disbelieved in their Rabb. Behold! May the Aad, the people of Hood ﵊ be distanced
v.s: And they were [therefore] followed in this world with a curse and [as well] on the Day of Resurrection. Unquestionably, ʿAad denied their Lord; then away with ʿAad, the people of Hūd.
v.c: They were followed by a curse in this world, as they will be on the Day of Judgment. Surely ’Âd denied their Lord. So away with ’Âd, the people of Hûd. Prophet Ṣâliḥ

q: Thamud We sent their brother Saalih ﵊
Allaah. There is no Ilaah for you besides Him. He created you from the earth and settled you on it. So seek forgiveness from Him, then turn to Him. Undoubtedly, my Rabb is Near, Responsive
v.s: And to Thamūd [We sent] their brother Sālih. He said, “O my people, worship God; you have no deity other than Him. He has produced you from the earth and settled you in it, so ask forgiveness of Him and then repent to Him. Indeed, my Lord is near and responsive.”
v.c: And to the people of Thamûd We sent their brother Ṣâliḥ. He said, “O my people! Worship Allah. You have no god other than Him. He ˹is the One Who˺ produced you from the earth and settled you on it. So seek His forgiveness and turn to Him in repentance. Surely my Lord is Ever Near, All-Responsive ˹to prayers˺.”

m: the one in whom hope was placed
q: They said, “O Saalih! Certainly we entertained high hopes in you before
(before you started preaching Towheed to us, we thought that you would be one of our leaders or a saint because of your wisdom and intellect).
Do you forbid us from worshipping what our forefathers worshipped? Surely we are in such doubt about what you call us towards that it has cast us into uncertainty.”
v.s: They said, “O Sālih, you were among us a man of promise before this. Do you forbid us to worship what our fathers worshipped? And indeed we are, about that to which you invite us, in disquieting doubt.”
v.c: They argued, “O Ṣâliḥ! We truly had high hopes in you before this. How dare you forbid us to worship what our forefathers had worshipped? We are certainly in alarming doubt about what you are inviting us to.”

q: He said, “O my people! Tell me. If I am upon a clear proof from my Rabb
(which proves that I am a Nabi)
and He has granted me a mercy
from Himself, who will assist me against
(by doing what pleases you and not conveying the message of Towheed that He has commanded me to convey)? (By discouraging me from doing what I have been commanded to do and asking me to follow you)
You only increase me in loss
(increase my misfortune because this will attract Allaah's punishment).”
v.s: He said, "O my people, have you considered: if I should be upon clear evidence from my Lord and He has given me mercy from Himself, who would protect me from God if I disobeyed Him? So you would not increase me except in loss.
v.c: He responded, “O my people! Consider if I stand on a clear proof from my Lord and He has blessed me with a mercy from Him. Who could help me against Allah if I were to disobey Him? You would only contribute to my doom.

q: (to prove to you that I am Allaah's Nabi).
So leave it to graze in Allaah's land and do not touch it with evil intent, for then a near
v.s: And O my people, this is the she-camel of God - [she is] to you a sign. So let her feed upon God's earth and do not touch her with harm, or you will be taken by an impending punishment."
v.c: And O my people! This she-camel of Allah is a sign for you. So leave her to graze ˹freely˺ on Allah’s earth and do her no harm, or a swift punishment will overtake you!”

q: said, “Enjoy yourselves in your homes for three days
(after which Allaah's punishment will destroy you).
This is a promise that will not prove false.”
v.s: But they hamstrung her, so he said, "Enjoy yourselves in your homes for three days. That is a promise not to be denied [i.e., unfailing]."
v.c: But they killed her, so he warned ˹them˺, “You have ˹only˺ three ˹more˺ days to enjoy life in your homes— this is an unfailing promise!”

q: came, We saved Saalih ﵊ and those who had Imaan with him by Our mercy and
from the humiliation of that day
(being the victim of Allaah's punishment is humiliating).
Indeed your Rabb is Powerful, the Mighty.
v.s: So when Our command came, We saved Sālih and those who believed with him, by mercy from Us, and [saved them] from the disgrace of that day. Indeed, it is your Lord who is the Powerful, the Exalted in Might.
v.c: When Our command came, We saved Ṣâliḥ and those who believed with him by a mercy from Us and spared them the disgrace of that Day. Surely your Lord ˹alone˺ is the All-Powerful, Almighty.

q: the oppressors and they were left lying face down in their homes...
v.s: And the shriek seized those who had wronged, and they became within their homes [corpses] fallen prone
v.c: And the ˹mighty˺ blast overtook the wrongdoers, so they fell lifeless in their homes,

q: ...as if they had never existed there. Behold! The Thamud disbelieved in
their Rabb. Behold! May the Thamud be distanced
v.s: As if they had never prospered therein. Unquestionably, Thamūd denied their Lord; then, away with Thamūd.
v.c: as if they had never lived there. Surely Thamûd denied their Lord, so away with Thamûd!

q: Indeed Our messenger angels came to Ibraheem ﵊ with good news
(that he will father a son and have grandsons afterwards)
and did not hesitate to bring a roasted calf
(to entertain them). (However, they did not partake of the meal because angels do not eat.)
v.s: And certainly did Our messengers [i.e., angels] come to Abraham with good tidings; they said, "Peace." He said, "Peace," and did not delay in bringing [them] a roasted calf.
v.c: And surely Our messenger-angels came to Abraham with good news ˹of a son˺. They greeted ˹him with˺, “Peace!” And he replied, “Peace ˹be upon you˺!” Then it was not long before he brought ˹them˺ a ˹fat,˺ roasted calf.

q: When he noticed that their hands were not reaching towards it
(thinking that they had come to harm him).
v.s: But when he saw their hands not reaching for it, he distrusted them and felt from them apprehension. They said, "Fear not. We have been sent to the people of Lot."
v.c: And when he saw that their hands did not reach for the food, he became suspicious and fearful of them. They reassured ˹him˺, “Do not be afraid! We are ˹angels˺ sent ˹only˺ against the people of Lot.”

m: Then We gave her glad tidings
q: as We conveyed to her the good news
(that she would be giving birth to a son by the name)
(that she will have a grandson by the name of)
v.s: And his wife was standing, and she smiled. Then We gave her good tidings of Isaac and after Isaac, Jacob.
v.c: And his wife was standing by, so she laughed, then We gave her good news of ˹the birth of˺ Isaac, and, after him, Jacob.

q: “Oh dear! Shall I bear a child when I am an old woman
and my husband here is an old man
This is indeed a strange event!”
v.s: She said, "Woe to me! Shall I give birth while I am an old woman and this, my husband, is an old man? Indeed, this is an amazing thing!"
v.c: She wondered, “Oh, my! How can I have a child in this old age, and my husband here is an old man? This is truly an astonishing thing!”

q: May Allaah's mercy and blessings be on you, O members of the household
Verily He is Worthy of all praise, The Exalted.”
v.s: They said, “Are you amazed at the decree of God? May the mercy of God and His blessings be upon you, people of the house. Indeed, He is Praiseworthy and Honourable.”
v.c: They responded, “Are you astonished by Allah’s decree? May Allah’s mercy and blessings be upon you, O people of this house. Indeed, He is Praiseworthy, All-Glorious.”

q: When the fear left Ibraheem ﵊ and the good news reached him, he pleaded with Us regarding the nation of Loot ﵊
(he debated that the angels should not destroy a city when there are Mu'mineen in it).
v.s: And when the fright had left Abraham and the good tidings had reached him, he began to argue [i.e., plead] with Us concerning the people of Lot.
v.c: Then after the fear had left Abraham, and the good news had reached him, he began to plead with Us for the people of Lot.

v.s: Indeed, Abraham was forbearing, grieving and [frequently] returning [to God].
v.c: Truly, Abraham was forbearing, tender-hearted, and ever turning ˹to his Lord˺.

q: (However, when the debate grew too long, the angels said)
Without doubt the command of your Rabb has come
There shall surely come to them a punishment that cannot be turned away.”
(Of course, the Mu'mineen and Loot ﵊ will be saved.)
v.s: [The angels said], "O Abraham, give up this [plea]. Indeed, the command of your Lord has come, and indeed, there will reach them a punishment that cannot be repelled."
v.c: ˹The angels said,˺ “O Abraham! Plead no more! Your Lord’s decree has already come, and they will certainly be afflicted with a punishment that cannot be averted!”

q: When Our messenger angels came to Loot ﵊, he became distressed because of their presence and his heart tightened
(because the angels appeared as handsome young men, Loot ﵊ feared that his people would want to commit sodomy with them).
He said, “This is a day of misfortune.”
v.s: And when Our messengers, [the angels], came to Lot, he was anguished for them and felt for them great discomfort and said, "This is a trying day."
v.c: When Our messenger-angels came to Lot, he was distressed and worried by their arrival. He said, “This is a terrible day.”

q: His people came running to him
(to see his guests). (This was nothing new because)
Before this they had always engaged in evil deeds
He said, “O my people! These daughters of mine
so fear Allaah and do not disgrace
me in front of my guests. Is there not a
v.s: And his people came hastening to him, and before [this] they had been doing evil deeds. He said, "O my people, these are my daughters; they are purer for you. So fear God and do not disgrace me concerning my guests. Is there not among you a man of reason?"
v.c: And ˹the men of˺ his people—who were used to shameful deeds—came to him rushing. He pleaded, “O my people! Here are my daughters ˹for marriage˺—they are pure for you. So fear Allah, and do not humiliate me by disrespecting my guests. Is there not ˹even˺ a single right-minded man among you?”

q: They replied, “You know very well that we have no interest in your daughters
You are also well aware of our intentions
v.s: They said, "You have already known that we have not concerning your daughters [i.e., women] any claim [i.e., desire], and indeed, you know what we want."
v.c: They argued, “You certainly know that we have no need for your daughters. You already know what we desire!”

q: He said, “If only I had some might
I could seek protection from a strong pillar
v.s: He said, "If only I had against you some power or could take refuge in a strong support."
v.c: He responded, “If only I had the strength ˹to resist you˺ or could rely on a strong supporter.”

q: The angels said, “O Loot! We are the messengers of your Rabb. They will never be able to reach
with your family during a portion of the night, and none should turn to look back; excepting your wife,
(do not take her with you because)
she will be afflicted with the same punishment that shall afflict them
(she had informed the people about the coming of their guests).
The morning has been fixed for the punishment. Is the morning not soon enough?”
v.s: They [the angels] said, "O Lot, indeed we are messengers of your Lord; [therefore], they will never reach you. So set out with your family during a portion of the night and let not any among you look back - except your wife; indeed, she will be struck by that which strikes them. Indeed, their appointment is [for] the morning. Is not the morning near?"
v.c: The angels said, “O Lot! We are the messengers of your Lord. They will never reach you. So travel with your family in the dark of night, and do not let any of you look back, except your wife. She will certainly suffer the fate of the others. Their appointed time is the morning. Is the morning not near?”

q: came, We made the upper portion of the land the lower portion
(the cities were lifted and then thrown upside down)
and We rained down on the land continuously falling stones of pottery clay...
v.s: So when Our command came, We made the highest part [of the city] its lowest and rained upon them stones of layered hard clay, [which were]
v.c: When Our command came, We turned the cities upside down and rained down on them clustered stones of baked clay,

q: (every stone bore the name of the person it was meant to strike).
are not far from the oppressors
(from the Mushrikeen of Makkah, who passed by them when they travelled to Shaam).
v.s: Marked from your Lord. And it [i.e., God's punishment] is not from the wrongdoers [very] far.
v.c: marked by your Lord ˹O Prophet˺. And these stones are not far from the ˹pagan˺ wrongdoers!

q: (the people living in the town of)
Madyan We sent their brother Shu'ayb ﵊
Allaah. There is no Ilaah for you besides Him. Do not reduce
(do not underweigh and undermeasure when trading).
Indeed I see you in fortunate
I fear for you the punishment of a day that will surround all
v.s: And to Madyan [We sent] their brother Shuʿayb. He said, "O my people, worship God; you have no deity other than Him. And do not decrease from the measure and the scale. Indeed, I see you in prosperity, but indeed, I fear for you the punishment of an all-encompassing Day.
v.c: And to the people of Midian We sent their brother Shu’aib. He said, “O my people! Worship Allah. You have no god other than Him. And do not give short measure and weight. I do see you in prosperity now, but I truly fear for you the torment of an overwhelming Day.

q: “O my people! Weigh and measure in full with justice, do not decrease for people their things
(do not give them less than they pay for)
and do not spread corruption on earth
(by committing kufr, Shirk and oppressing people).”
v.s: And O my people, give full measure and weight in justice and do not deprive the people of their due and do not commit abuse on the earth, spreading corruption.
v.c: O my people! Give full measure and weigh with justice. Do not defraud people of their property, nor go about spreading corruption in the land.

q: (after you have given others what is due to them)
(than the excess that you wrongfully take from them)
v.s: What remains [lawful] from God is best for you, if you would be believers. But I am not a guardian over you."
v.c: What is left ˹as a lawful gain˺ by Allah is far better for you if you are ˹truly˺ believers. And I am not a keeper over you.”

q: They said, “O Shu'ayb! Does your salaah
that we leave what our forefathers worshipped or
(does it instruct you to tell us that we should leave)
doing as we please with our wealth? Surely you are
v.s: They said, "O Shuʿayb, does your prayer [i.e., religion] command you that we should leave what our fathers worship or not do with our wealth what we please? Indeed, you are the forbearing, the discerning!"
v.c: They asked ˹sarcastically˺, “O Shu’aib! Does your prayer command you that we should abandon what our forefathers worshipped or give up managing our wealth as we please? Indeed, you are such a tolerant, sensible man!”

m: as much as I am able
as much as I am able
q: Shu'ayb ﵊ said, “O my people! Tell me. If I am on a clear proof from my Rabb
(which proves that I am His Nabi)
and He provides a bountiful provision for me,
(then how can I stop preaching Towheed to you?).
I do not wish to oppose you in a manner that I do the same things that I forbid you from doing
(I shall therefore never instruct you to do anything that I am not willing to do myself. So accept what I tell you without fear).
reformation as far as I am able
My ability is only from Allaah. Only on Him do I rely and only to Him do I turn.”
v.s: He said, "O my people, have you considered: if I am upon clear evidence from my Lord and He has provided me with a good provision from Him...? And I do not intend to differ from you in that which I have forbidden you; I only intend reform as much as I am able. And my success is not but through God. Upon Him I have relied, and to Him I return.
v.c: He said, “O my people! Consider if I stand on a clear proof from my Lord and He has blessed me with a good provision from Him. I do not want to do what I am forbidding you from. I only intend reform to the best of my ability. My success comes only through Allah. In Him I trust and to Him I turn.

q: “O my people! Let not your opposition for me
cause the same punishment to afflict you as afflicted the nation of Nooh ﵊ or the nation of Hood ﵊ or the nation of Saalih ﵊. And the nation of Loot were not far off from you
v.s: And O my people, let not [your] dissension from me cause you to be struck by that similar to what struck the people of Noah or the people of Hūd or the people of Sālih. And the people of Lot are not from you far away.
v.c: O my people! Do not let your opposition to me lead you to a fate similar to that of the people of Noah, or Hûd, or Ṣâliḥ. And the people of Lot are not far from you.

q: “Seek forgiveness from your Rabb then turn to Him. Indeed my Rabb is Most Merciful, Most Loving
v.s: And ask forgiveness of your Lord and then repent to Him. Indeed, my Lord is Merciful and Affectionate."
v.c: So seek your Lord’s forgiveness and turn to Him in repentance. Surely my Lord is Most Merciful, All-Loving.”

m: surely we would have stoned you
q: said, “O Shu'ayb! We do not understand much of what you say, and we consider you to be a weakling among us. If it were not for your tribe
we would have certainly stoned you. You are not deserving of
v.s: They said, "O Shuʿayb, we do not understand much of what you say, and indeed, we consider you among us as weak. And if not for your family, we would have stoned you [to death]; and you are not to us one respected."
v.c: They threatened, “O Shu’aib! We do not comprehend much of what you say, and surely we see you powerless among us. Were it not for your clan, we would have certainly stoned you, for you are nothing to us.”

q: said, “O my people! Is my tribe more deserving of honour to you than Allaah Whom you have cast behind your backs
(you have regard for me only because of the tribe I belong to rather than because of the fact that I am Allaah's Nabi)?
Verily my Rabb surrounds all that you do
(He knows all that you do and will take you to task for it for you can never escape His grasp).'
v.s: He said, "O my people, is my family more respected for power by you than God? But you put Him behind your backs [in neglect]. Indeed, my Lord is encompassing of what you do.
v.c: He said, “O my people! Do you have more regard for my clan than for Allah, turning your back on Him entirely? Surely my Lord is Fully Aware of what you do.

q: “O my people! Carry out your actions as you are
I too am carrying out my actions. Soon you shall come to know to whom
such a punishment come that will disgrace him, and
who is a liar. Keep waiting
(to see which of us is right).
Indeed I am waiting with you
v.s: And O my people, work according to your position; indeed, I am working. You are going to know to whom will come a punishment that will disgrace him and who is a liar. So watch; indeed, I am with you a watcher, [awaiting the outcome]."
v.c: O my people! Persist in your ways, for I ˹too˺ will persist in mine. You will soon come to know who will be visited by a humiliating torment and is a liar! And watch! I too am watching with you!”

q: Shu'ayb ﵊ and those who had Imaan with him by Our mercy. A scream seized
the oppressors and they lay face down in their homes...
v.s: And when Our command came, We saved Shuʿayb and those who believed with him, by mercy from Us. And the shriek seized those who had wronged, and they became within their homes [corpses] fallen prone
v.c: When Our command came, We saved Shu’aib and those who believed with him by a mercy from Us. And the ˹mighty˺ blast overtook the wrongdoers, so they fell lifeless in their homes,

q: just as the Thamud were distanced
v.s: As if they had never prospered therein. Then, away with Madyan as Thamūd was taken away.
v.c: as if they had never lived there. So away with Midian as it was with Thamûd!

q: Verily We sent Moosa ﵊ with Our Aayaat
v.s: And We did certainly send Moses with Our signs and a clear authority
v.c: Indeed, We sent Moses with Our signs and compelling proof

q: they followed the orders of Fir'oun, and the orders of Fir'oun were improper
(which led them to their destruction in both worlds).
v.s: To Pharaoh and his establishment, but they followed the command of Pharaoh, and the command of Pharaoh was not [at all] discerning.
v.c: to Pharaoh and his chiefs, but they followed the command of Pharaoh, and Pharaoh’s command was not well guided.

q: will lead his people on the Day of Qiyaamah and
(since they will follow him as they did in this world, he will)
(of Jahannam, just as they followed him into the cold water that drowned them).
It is an evil place indeed where they shall be entered.
v.s: He will precede his people on the Day of Resurrection and lead them into the Fire; and wretched is the place to which they are led.
v.c: He will be before his people on the Day of Judgment and will lead them into the Fire. What an evil place to be led into!

q: has been made to follow them
in this world and in the Aakhirah as well. It will be an evil prize
v.s: And they were followed in this [world] with a curse and on the Day of Resurrection. And wretched is the gift which is given.
v.c: They were followed by a curse in this ˹life˺ and ˹will receive another˺ on the Day of Judgment. What an evil gift to receive!

q: is from the narratives of the cities that We relate to you
Some of them are still standing, while others have been harvested
v.s: That is from the news of the cities, which We relate to you; of them, some are [still] standing and some are [as] a harvest [mowed down].
v.c: These are accounts, We relate to you ˹O Prophet˺, of the ˹destroyed˺ cities. Some are still standing ˹barren˺, while others have been mowed down.

q: (by inviting Allaah's punishment when they committed Shirk).
Their gods which they called upon
besides Allaah were of no benefit to them at all when the command
(because they were punished according to the extent to which they worshipped these gods).
v.s: And We did not wrong them, but they wronged themselves. And they were not availed at all by their gods which they invoked other than God when there came the command of your Lord. And they did not increase them in other than ruin.
v.c: We did not wrong them, rather they wronged themselves. The gods they invoked beside Allah were of no help at all when the command of your Lord came, and only contributed to their ruin.

q: of your Rabb when He seized a town that is oppressive
v.s: And thus is the seizure of your Lord when He seizes the cities while they are committing wrong. Indeed, His seizure is painful and severe.
v.c: Such is the ˹crushing˺ grip of your Lord when He seizes the societies entrenched in wrongdoing. Indeed, His grip is ˹terribly˺ painful and severe.

q: for him who fears the punishment of the Aakhirah. That
shall be a day when people will be gathered
(on the Plain of Reckoning to account for their actions)
and that will be the day when all will be present
(no one will be able to absent himself).
v.s: Indeed in that is a sign for those who fear the punishment of the Hereafter. That is a Day for which the people will be collected, and that is a Day [which will be] witnessed.
v.c: Surely in this is a sign for those who fear the torment of the Hereafter. That is a Day for which humanity will be gathered and a Day ˹that will be˺ witnessed ˹by all˺.

q: (so that it occurs only when Allaah has destined it to be).
v.s: And We do not delay it except for a limited term.
v.c: We only delay it for a fixed term.

q: will dawn, a soul will speak only with Allaah's permission. Some of them
will be unfortunate, while others will be fortunate.
v.s: The Day it comes no soul will speak except by His permission. And among them will be the wretched and the prosperous.
v.c: When that Day arrives, no one will dare speak except with His permission. Some of them will be miserable, others joyful.

q: As for those who will be unfortunate, they will certainly be in the Fire, where they will scream and shout
(with sounds resembling the braying of a donkey).
v.s: As for those who were [destined to be] wretched, they will be in the Fire. For them therein is [violent] exhaling and inhaling.
v.c: As for those bound for misery, they will be in the Fire, where they will be sighing and gasping,

q: They will live there forever as long as the skies and the earth exist

(if Allaah wills that the period be shortened, He may shorten it for whom He wills. However, Allaah will not all owt a Kaafir to emerge from Jahannam because eternal punishment has been promised for him).
Undoubtedly your Rabb can perfectly accomplish whatever He wills.
v.s: [They will be] abiding therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except what your Lord should will. Indeed, your Lord is an effecter of what He intends.
v.c: staying there forever, as long as the heavens and the earth will endure, except what your Lord wills. Surely your Lord does what He intends.

q: As for those who will be fortunate, they will certainly be in Jannah, where they will live forever, as long as the skies and the earth exist, except as your Rabb wills

(if Allaah wills that the period be shortened, He may shorten it for whom He wills. However, Allaah will not will that a Mu'min should emerge from Jannah because eternal happiness has been promised for him).
v.s: And as for those who were [destined to be] prosperous, they will be in Paradise, abiding therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except what your Lord should will - a bestowal uninterrupted.
v.c: And as for those destined to joy, they will be in Paradise, staying there forever, as long as the heavens and the earth will endure, except what your Lord wills—a ˹generous˺ giving, without end.

m: will surely pay them in full
q: So do not be in doubt about what
(worshipping their gods will certainly earn them Allaah's punishment).
They merely worship as their forefathers worshipped before
(and will therefore suffer the same fate as their forefathers).
Verily We shall grant them their full share
v.s: So do not be in doubt, [O Muhammad], as to what these [polytheists] are worshipping. They worship not except as their fathers worshipped before. And indeed, We will give them their share undiminished.
v.c: So do not be in doubt ˹O Prophet˺ about what those ˹pagans˺ worship. They worship nothing except what their forefathers worshipped before ˹them˺. And We will certainly give them their share ˹of punishment˺ in full, without any reduction.

q: Indeed We had granted Moosa ﵊ the Book
after which differences arose about it
If it were not for a word
(that they will be punished in the Aakhirah),
(that they should be punished in this world)
would have been passed between them. They are in such
doubt about it that they have been cast into uncertainty
(and cannot determine fact from fallacy or the truth from falsehood).
v.s: And We had certainly given Moses the Scripture, but it came under disagreement. And if not for a word that preceded from your Lord, it would have been judged between them. And indeed they are, concerning it [i.e., the Qur’ān], in disquieting doubt.
v.c: Indeed, We had given Moses the Scripture, but differences arose regarding it. Had it not been for a prior decree from your Lord, their differences would have been settled ˹at once˺. They are truly in alarming doubt about it.

m: surely will pay them in full
q: Without doubt your Rabb will certainly grant the full recompense
for the actions of every person there may be. Indeed He is Informed of whatever they do.
v.s: And indeed, each [of the believers and disbelievers] - your Lord will fully compensate them for their deeds. Indeed, He is Acquainted with what they do.
v.c: And surely your Lord will fully pay all for their deeds. He is certainly All-Aware of what they do.

q: as you have been commanded and
and do not transgress the limits. Surely He sees what you do.
v.s: So remain on a right course as you have been commanded, [you] and those who have turned back with you [to God], and do not transgress. Indeed, He is Seeing of what you do.
v.c: So be steadfast as you are commanded ˹O Prophet˺, along with those who turn ˹in submission to Allah˺ with you. And do not transgress. Surely He is All-Seeing of what you ˹believers˺ do.

q: (do not associate with and do not imitate)
shall reach you and you will not have any helpers
Allaah and you will not be assisted
v.s: And do not incline toward those who do wrong, lest you be touched by the Fire, and you would not have other than God any protectors; then you would not be helped.
v.c: And do not be inclined to the wrongdoers or you will be touched by the Fire. For then you would have no protectors other than Allah, nor would you be helped.

q: Establish salaah at the two ends of the day
(with Fajr salaah and Zuhr salaah at the one end and Asr salaah and Maghrib salaah at the other)
and during portions of the night
wipe out evil acts. This is advice to those who will take heed
v.s: And establish prayer at the two ends of the day and at the approach of the night. Indeed, good deeds do away with misdeeds. That is a reminder for those who remember.
v.c: Establish prayer ˹O Prophet˺ at both ends of the day and in the early part of the night. Surely good deeds wipe out evil deeds. That is a reminder for the mindful.

q: for undoubtedly Allaah does not put to waste
the reward of those who do good.
v.s: And be patient, for indeed, God does not allow to be lost the reward of those who do good.
v.c: And be patient! Certainly Allah does not discount the reward of the good-doers.

q: Besides a few of them whom We had rescued
why were there no more men of understanding from the nations of the past who would prevent
(However, instead of preventing others from kufr)
(they also did what the others did). (Had people prevented others from kufr, they would have all been saved from Allaah's punishment which comes when good souls are outnumbered).
v.s: So why were there not among the generations before you those of enduring discrimination forbidding corruption on earth - except a few of those We saved from among them? But those who wronged pursued what luxury they were given therein, and they were criminals.
v.c: If only there had been among the ˹destroyed˺ peoples before you, ˹O believers,˺ virtuous individuals who forbade corruption in the land—other than the few We had saved ˹from the torment˺. But the wrongdoers ˹only˺ pursued their ˹worldly˺ pleasures, becoming wicked.

q: of your Rabb to destroy cities unjustly when their inhabitants engaged in reformation
(Allaah does not destroy people when they are Mu'mineen, actively reforming themselves and others and making an effort to spread their Deen).
v.s: And your Lord would not have destroyed the cities unjustly while their people were reformers.
v.c: And your Lord ˹O Prophet˺ would never destroy a society unjustly while its people were acting rightly.

q: If your Rabb had willed, He would have made all people a single nation
(all practising the correct Deen. However, He did not intend this for reasons best known to Him). (Therefore,)
v.s: And if your Lord had willed, He could have made mankind one community; but they will not cease to differ,
v.c: Had your Lord so willed, He would have certainly made humanity one single community ˹of believers˺, but they will always ˹choose to˺ differ—

q: ...except those on whom your Rabb has mercy
(such people will conscientiously follow the teachings of the Ambiyaa without question). (Do not grieve about this because)
Allaah had created them for this.
(They are meant to dispute in this world because)
The decree of your Rabb shall certainly be fulfilled:
“I will definitely fill Jahannam with multitudes of man and Jinn.”
(Therefore, there will always be people who deserve to enter Jahannam.)
v.s: Except whom your Lord has given mercy, and for that He created them. But the word of your Lord is to be fulfilled that, "I will surely fill Hell with jinn and men all together."
v.c: except those shown mercy by your Lord—and so He created them ˹to choose freely˺. And so the Word of your Lord will be fulfilled: “I will surely fill up Hell with jinn and humans all together.”

q: all the narratives of the Rusul so that your heart may be strengthened
(so that you may take courage from them).
has come to you, as well as advice and a reminder for the Mu'mineen.
v.s: And each [story] We relate to you from the news of the messengers is that by which We make firm your heart. And there has come to you, in this, the truth and an instruction and a reminder for the believers.
v.c: And We relate to you ˹O Prophet˺ the stories of the messengers to reassure your heart. And there has come to you in this ˹sûrah˺ the truth, a warning ˹to the disbelievers˺, and a reminder to the believers.

q: Tell those who do not have Imaan, “Continue performing acts as you are
v.s: And say to those who do not believe, "Work according to your position; indeed, we are working.
v.c: Say to those who disbelieve, “Persist in your ways; we will certainly persist in ours.

v.s: And wait; indeed, we are waiting."
v.c: And wait! Surely we ˹too˺ are waiting.”

q: To Allaah belongs the unseen things of the heavens and the earth and to Him Alone will all matters return
(in the Aakhirah when He will take people to task for what they did).
Him and rely on Him only.
Your Rabb is not unaware of what you do.
v.s: And to God belong the unseen [aspects] of the heavens and the earth and to Him will be returned the matter, all of it, so worship Him and rely upon Him. And your Lord is not unaware of that which you do.
v.c: To Allah ˹alone˺ belongs the knowledge of what is hidden in the heavens and the earth. And to Him all matters are returned. So worship Him and put your trust in Him. And your Lord is never unaware of what you do.
